subject: Processing location visibility and erase commitments — prospect Q&A
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@edgework.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Qs on where our inference traffic is processed / deletion paths

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — EdgeWork's security team asked for a short written Q&A so we can validate whether Redwood's hosted inference will meet our residency and deletion commitments. High-level items they want answered:

1) Where will request payloads (prompts + any uploaded context) be processed geographically when using Redwood hosted API? Please list regions and any conditions that cause cross-border hops.
2) Which subprocessors are involved in the request path (runtime, autoscaling, monitoring, logging, metrics, storage) and in which countries they operate?
3) What is the retention policy for transient caches (KV cache, prefix cache) vs. persistent logs/telemetry? How quickly can data be fully erased on request?
4) Do you support an EU-only execution plane (no egress to US) for customers, and if so, what are the constraints?
5) Any material export-control or government access considerations we should be aware of?

If you can provide a short narrative plus any evidence artifacts (subprocessor inventory, sample SOP for deletion) that would be ideal. We may share with procurement.

Thanks — appreciate concise answers we can hand to our InfoSec reviewer.

—Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Security, EdgeWork AI

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@edgework.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-01T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where our inference traffic is processed / deletion paths

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below is a short summary; Karhtik and Marissa are looped in for the detailed evidence and operational notes (we've attached two stubs here to illustrate the kinds of artifacts we share).

1) Processing geography: Hosted API routes requests to nearest-capacity by default. Primary execution regions we operate: us-west-2 (US), eu-central-1 (EU), asia-southeast-1 (APAC). For customers that do not pin a region, requests typically execute in the region nearest the caller, but policy routing (cost/latency/fallback) can cause cross-region hops. Cross-border hops occur only when a regional capacity is unavailable and the configured routing policy allows fallback; for regulated customers we offer region-pin and strict no-fallback options.

2) Subprocessors: Runtime (Redwood runtime) - managed by Redwood, primarily in the execution region; Cloud infra (AWS/GCP) - varies by region; Monitoring/telemetry - Datadog (metrics) in US/EU; S3-compatible object storage for logs (region-scoped buckets); KMS providers for encryption keys (customer-managed KMS supported). We will provide a CSV inventory with country mappings (attached stub).

3) Retention & deletion: Ephemeral per-request state (LLM KV cache, temporary tensors) is discarded immediately after the request completes; prefix/KV caches are time-bounded — default TTL is 1 hour, configurable down to 0. For hosted customers using our default settings, cached prefixes may be retained up to 24 hours for performance; persistent logs (request metadata, billing traces) are retained 90 days by default. On a subject access / erasure request, we initiate an erase workflow within 24 hours and complete deletion of customer content from active stores within 30 days; full removal from backups (if any) follows the backup retention schedule (up to 90 days) unless otherwise contractually scoped.

4) EU-only execution: Yes — we offer an EU-only hosted tenancy that pins execution to eu-central-1 and disables cross-region fallback, plus an option for Dedicated/Private deployment in customer VPC to ensure no egress. Constraints: model availability may be narrower (we only host verified model variants in-region) and throughput commitments differ; pricing and SLA terms vary.

5) Export controls / government access: We operate under standard cloud provider legal frameworks. For customers in regulated industries we recommend Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and customer-managed KMS. We will provide our SOC 2 scope and exporter guidance link.

Attached: residency-evidence-stub.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-stub.csv (real artifacts provided under NDA or as part of procurement). Karhtik will follow up with the technical evidence and a short erasure playbook.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

• When you say "ephemeral per-request state" is discarded immediately, does that include any intermediate cache entries created during streaming responses?
• For the erase workflow: can you confirm whether audit logs (who called what API) are ever treated as containing customer prompt content, or are they metadata-only?
• If we choose EU-only hosted tenancy, is there a standard way to demonstrate (audit artifact) that no cross-border egress occurred for a given time window?

If you can point to the specific evidence artifacts or SOP sections that cover those three bullets, that would help move this to procurement.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@edgework.ai>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-03T10:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where our inference traffic is processed / deletion paths

Alex — quick technical follow-up addressing each bullet, copying the SOP references we've uploaded to the Drive link above.

• Streaming / intermediate caches: Streaming responses may create short-lived fragments in our runtime process memory and transient KV shards. These fragments are not persisted to disk by default; they are removed from memory immediately after the stream completes. If a customer opts into prefix caching (for prompt reuse), those entries are stored in an in-region cache with configurable TTL; we can set TTL=0 for strict non-retention. See SOP section: "Runtime Cache Controls (SOP 4.3)".

• Audit logs: Our telemetry captures API call metadata (request size, latency, model, route) and a hash fingerprint of the request payload for deduplication/traceability. We do not write full prompt content into telemetry indices. Full request content is only stored in short-lived request stores used for debugging when a customer explicitly enables request logging; that feature is off by default and requires customer consent. See SOP section: "Logging & Debug Mode (SOP 3.1)".

• EU-only audit artifact: For EU-only tenancy customers we produce an execution manifest for any date range that lists per-request execution region and the set of instances that executed the request (instance ids and region). That manifest is generated from our runtime routing logs and signed by our ops team; it is suitable for audits and procurement evidence. For Private deployments, we can additionally provide network flow captures under NDA. See Drive: residency-evidence/DW-2248/manifest-sample.csv.

Operational notes / commitments:
- Erase workflow initiation: within 24 hours of a validated erasure request.
- Active-store purge: completed within 30 days (we provide a signed statement of completion for procurement).
- Backup/backfill windows: up to 90 days unless contract specifies otherwise.
- KMS: we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys (CMKs) in-region; CMKs are recommended for maximum data sovereignty.

If EdgeWork would like, we can schedule a short 30-minute call with our runtime engineering lead to walk through the manifest generation and the SOP excerpts.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
